sources.entry: Gifcurry - Video to GIF maker with a graphical interface capable of cropping, adding text, seeking, and trimming.

summary.one_liner: Gifcurry is an open-source, Haskell-built video editor that converts videos into GIFs (or videos) with a GUI, a CLI, and a Haskell library API.
summary.what_it_does: Loads a video file in any of most common formats and lets you trim start and end times, crop from the left, right, top, and bottom, and add text overlays with adjustable font, size, color, position, outline, rotation, and timing. Output can be a GIF or a video, with settings for width, frames per second, color count, and dithering. The command line tool (gifcurry_cli) exposes the same options and can take a YAML text overlay file or an SRT subtitles file. The README says the program hides the underlying FFmpeg and ImageMagick details from the user.
use_cases: Convert a video clip into a GIF
Add meme text to a GIF
Crop and trim a screen recording for a README or pull request
Batch GIF creation from the command line
Add subtitles to a video from an SRT file
Make a short looping animation for chat or email
how_to_run: Linux: download the AppImage from the releases page, mark it executable, and double-click it
Mac: run the gifcurry-mac-install-script.command from the Downloads folder (chmod +x, then ./gifcurry-mac-install-script.command)
Haskell developers: git clone the repo, cd gifcurry, stack setup, stack install alex happy, stack install gtk2hs-buildtools, stack install hsc2hs, stack install
Arch: install dependencies via pacman, then makepkg -sic from the cloned repo
notable: Command-line tool (gifcurry_cli) with full options, plus a GUI and a Haskell library API
Text overlays with font, outline, fill color, rotation, and timing controls, configurable through a YAML file
Can save output as a video instead of a GIF
Ships as AppImage, snap, and Mac install script
caveats: Requires external dependencies (FFmpeg, GStreamer, ImageMagick, GTK+) to be installed
The README says Windows support is 'most likely' but not confirmed
The snap includes only the GUI; the CLI requires a separate download
Building from source requires Haskell Stack and several extra build tools
